member.remarks: If you assign an imagelist from this class to a control, it must be removed from that control in the owning dialog's Dispose method. Failure to do this will result in the inability for .NET to Garbage Collect the dialog, and all controls within it.

member.name: T:OSIsoft.AF.UI.AFPlugInEditor
member.summary: Provides access to configuration dialogs provided by the various AFPlugIns.
member.remarks:
If required, the plug-ins will be downloaded to the client machine. If the plug-in supports its own dialog for editing its configuration, that can be accessed via the DataReferenceModal, AnalysisRuleModal and TimeRuleModal methods. If the plug-in does not support its own dialog, these methods will provide a standard property grid editor for editing the plug-in's defined properties.
The DataReferenceProperties, AnlysisRuleProperties, and TimeRuleProperties methods will always use the standard property grid editor. If one is supplied in the call, then these methods will behave in a modeless fashion.
The property grid editor in Microsoft.NET relies on the use of attributes on the properties in the class definition. These attributes are fully described in the System.ComponentModel documentation and are illustrated in the AF SDK Developers Toolkit.

The UpdateNameTextBox method is called if the mAFObject inherits from a template, has a name pattern and the control used for the name is currently not in an edit state.

member.name: M:OSIsoft.AF.UI.AFTreeView.AFSelect(System.Object,System.Object,System.String)
member.summary: Selects the object in the tree.
member.param: The object to select.

The context of the selection. When an item can appear in multiple places in the tree, the context aids in selecting the correct location. When a context is provided, the selection mechanism will prefer finding the specified afobject under tree node represented by the context.
A path to the object can server as a backup mechanism for finding the specified object, or, can be used when the object could appear in multiple places in the tree.

member.name: M:OSIsoft.AF.UI.AFTreeView.AFSelect(System.Object,System.Object,System.Object,System.String)
member.summary: Selects the object in the tree.
member.param: The object to select.

The context of the selection. When an item can appear in multiple places in the tree, the context aids in selecting the correct location. When a context is provided, the selection mechanism will prefer finding the specified afobject under tree node represented by the context.
A filter which limits where the object may be found at. For example, a category when selecting elements.
A path to the object can server as a backup mechanism for finding the specified object, or, can be used when the object could appear in multiple places in the tree.

member.name: M:OSIsoft.AF.UI.AFTreeView.AFSelectNext(System.Object,System.String)
member.summary: Select the next node to be shown in the tree.
member.param: The object to select in the tree.
The path to the object, in case the tree is unable to locate the object otherwise.
member.remarks: Use this method to delay the selection of the next node until the application becomes idle. By delaying the selection, it can allow for other controls to completely finish processing their events before changing the tree selection, and potentially removing controls that are still in the process of handling the currently queued up events. Additionally, if multiple selection changes are queued, only the final selection is ultimately processed.

member.remarks: Implement this interface on a plug-in editor to enable several editor instances from the same plug-in shown in the same UI to share some UI component. This can be used, for example for two analysis rules of the same type to share toolkit UI.

member.name: P:OSIsoft.AF.UI.IAFSharablePlugInEditor.SharedEditor
member.summary: Gets or sets the shared editor for the plug-in editor.
member.remarks: Setting the shared editor should dissociate the plug-in editor from any other shared editors. Setting this property might cause the control to change its appearance (because it can delegate some shared functionality to the shared editor). This property should never be set to an instance of a type other than that returned by .
